<description>
Per the discussion in #35645, this PR adds a Python utility that performs the multisig setup process, so that RPC and interface work is shaped by what that flow actually needs.

It covers wallet creation, key generation at the BIP 87 path, collecting cosigner keys, assembling a `wsh(sortedmulti())` or `tr(musig(),sortedmulti_a())` descriptor, verifying it, and importing it.

### Gaps that need new functionality in C++
- `importdescriptors` rejects a descriptor with no private keys when the wallet has private keys enabled. See #35377.
- The wallet stores a multipath descriptor as two descriptors, so listdescriptors never shows the descriptor that was shared. See #36133.
- The wallet labels addresses, not keys, so cosigner names live in the setup and are lost on import.
- There is no RPC for validating a key expression, so the key is wrapped in `pkh()` for `getdescriptorinfo` to parse. See #35918, which exposes `ParsePubkey()`.
- `createmultisig` only takes plain public keys, not extended keys with origins, and cannot build a ranged or taproot multisig descriptor.
- Nothing reports what a descriptor commits to, or whether this wallet holds one of its keys, before it is imported.

Part of #35645.
</description>

[2026-10-23] c:6373344413 comment by pseudoramdom (member):
Thanks for putting this together and listing the gaps.

That said, I'm leaning Concept NACK on merging this into the repo.
The goal of #35645 is for the wallet to handle multisig setup by itself - a GUI wizard on top of `interfaces::Wallet`, plus the RPCs behind it. Like you said that work would supersede this script.  Merging this would mean reviewing ~700 lines (script and functional test) whose job is to work around things we plan to fix. We'd then have to review again each time one of those fixes lands and removes a workaround. I'd rather prefer we direct our resources at implementing items in #35645, since they reach both RPC and GUI users.

Also putting a script in `contrib/` makes it look like a recommended tool and that's hard to undo once people use it with real funds.

What we can do
- We can track this separately in a separate fork/gist and have it linked from #35645, so people testing the backend PRs can use it. As @sedited mentioned, it works fine as an external script.
- We can add the gaps from the description to #35645, so the Core backend work tracks them directly. Some are already there (#35377, #35918, `createmultisigdescriptor`, `analyzeDescriptor`)
